entries.title: Enough at home, still eager for a bite
entries.literal_meaning: A son from a well-fed household, yet eager for food!
entries.explanation: The teasing surprise lies in the mismatch: food is plentiful at home, yet the child lights up at the sight of something to eat. Here ରଙ୍କ carries eagerness for food, rather than the stinginess it carries in another saying on the same dictionary page. Spoken warmly, the line can notice the temptation of a fresh treat even after a meal; spoken sharply, it can embarrass the child. The joke is about that moment, not proof of a child’s character or whether they are hungry.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘରେ ଖାଇବାର ଅଭାବ ନାହିଁ, ତଥାପି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଦେଖି ପିଲାର ଆଗ୍ରହ ବଢ଼ିଯାଉଛି—ଏହି ଫରକରେ କଥାଟିର ଥଟ୍ଟା। ଏଠି ରଙ୍କ କହିଲେ କଞ୍ଜୁସ ନୁହେଁ, ଖାଇବା ପାଇଁ ଲାଳାୟିତ ହେବାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଖାଇସାରିଥିଲେ ବି ନୂଆ ଜଳଖିଆ ଦେଖି ମନ ବଳିବା ବେଳେ ଆଦରରେ ଏହି କଥା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ; କଟୁ ସ୍ୱରରେ କହିଲେ ସେଇ କଥା ପିଲାକୁ ଲଜ୍ଜିତ କରିପାରେ। ଏକ ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତର ଆଗ୍ରହ ଦେଖି ପିଲାର ସ୍ୱଭାବ କିମ୍ବା ତାକୁ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ତାହାର ରାୟ ଦେବା ଏହି ଥଟ୍ଟାର କାମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A teasing contrast between having enough food at home and eagerly wanting another treat.
entries.odia_summary: ଘରେ ଖାଇବା ଥାଇ ବି ଆଉ ଏକ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଆଗ୍ରହ ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ନେଇ ଥଟ୍ଟା।
entries.usage_example: After lunch, a child eagerly asks what is in a newly opened snack box. An aunt smiles and says, “ଖାଇଲାଘରର ପୁଅ ରଙ୍କ!” She then asks whether the child would like a little now or later. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: The source explicitly describes children in households where food is not lacking. The affectionate scene and discussion of tone are editorial, not observed testimony. Preserve the source’s son wording without making hunger or eagerness a gendered or innate trait. Distinct from 190’s stinginess and 191’s restricted choice.

entries.title: The claim of knowing three births
entries.literal_meaning: A poor person knows the story of three births.
entries.explanation: The line sounds like a claim to remarkable knowledge, but the dictionary supplies a harsh explanation. It attributes present poverty to not giving charity in a previous birth, then predicts poverty in the next birth from not giving in the present one. The three births connect alleged past conduct, present hardship and a predicted future; the gloss does not say that the person was poor in the previous birth. This is a recorded belief, not evidence explaining anyone’s poverty. Read critically, the saying shows how a neat turn of speech can make blame sound like settled knowledge.
entries.meaning_odia: ତିନି ଜନ୍ମର କଥା ଜାଣିବା ଶୁଣିଲେ ଅସାଧାରଣ ଜ୍ଞାନର କଥା ମନେ ହୁଏ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଅଛି ଏକ କଠୋର ବିଶ୍ୱାସ। ସେହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ପୂର୍ବ ଜନ୍ମରେ ଦାନ ନକରିବାକୁ ଏ ଜନ୍ମର ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟର କାରଣ କହେ, ଆଉ ଏ ଜନ୍ମରେ ଦାନ ନକରିବାରୁ ପର ଜନ୍ମରେ ବି ଦରିଦ୍ର ହେବ ବୋଲି କଳ୍ପନା କରେ। ପୂର୍ବ ଜନ୍ମରେ ସେ ଦରିଦ୍ର ଥିଲା ବୋଲି ସ୍ରୋତ କହେ ନାହିଁ। ଏହା ଲିପିବଦ୍ଧ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ, କାହାର ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟର ପ୍ରମାଣିତ କାରଣ ନୁହେଁ। କଥାଟିକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଦେଖାଯାଏ, ଏକ ଚତୁର ଉକ୍ତି କିପରି ଅଭାବରେ ଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଦୋଷ ଲଦି ତାହାକୁ ଜ୍ଞାନ ପରି ଶୁଣାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: The recorded belief blames present poverty on past-life non-giving and predicts future poverty from non-giving now; this explanation questions that claim.
entries.odia_summary: ପୂର୍ବ ଜନ୍ମର ଦାନ ନକରିବା ସହ ଏବର ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟକୁ, ଏବର ଦାନ ନକରିବା ସହ ପର ଜନ୍ମର ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ୁଥିବା ବିଶ୍ୱାସକୁ ଏଠି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: In a reading group, someone quotes “ରଙ୍କ ତିନି ଜନମ କଥା ଜାଣେ” and reads the dictionary gloss aloud. Another reader asks, “How could we know someone’s past birth—and why should their present hardship be taken as evidence against them?” (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: Critical historical documentation, not a recommended reproach to use against poor people. The source gives a karma/charity explanation explicitly; no observed past-life fact, empirical cause of poverty, general Odia belief or present community endorsement is established. The critical reading is Project Odisha’s editorial response.
